as_told.title: Bill Lear as neighbor and witness of Brown's experiments

plain: The aircraft maker Bill Lear is said to have worked right across the street from the inventor Thomas Townsend Brown in Santa Monica, California, and to have known him well. Brown's daughter Linda Brown remembers it first-hand: "We used to walk across There was a little diner right across the street," recalling lunches with Lear. She places it in the 1960s. Michels tells it in his own words in another episode, and dates it to the 1950s. In his version Lear's office was "right across the street" from Brown's company, Guidance Technologies. Michels casts Lear as someone who saw Brown's experiments, not just a lunch companion. Brown is a figure the subject ties to early work on craft that fly without propellers or jets. If true, one of America's best-known aviation men had a close view of that work.
